CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 3
TIME TO INVEST —
WHY CALDAS DA RAINHA — A CITY IN TRANSFORMATION
In a rapidly changing global economy, cities must be able to adapt to uncertainty, build resilience and  
embrace change without losing their identity. Success depends on turning that adaptability into tangible 
results.
Supply chains are moving closer to Europe, while energy and digital technologies are reshaping industry. 
Skilled professionals increasingly seek places where they can enjoy a high quality of life while building  
rewarding careers. Caldas da Rainha is responding to these changes. A defence technology company  
established here has become a unicorn. German industrial investors recognised the quality of our  
technical expertise years ago. And the European Commission named our city the 2026 European Capital 
of Small Retail.
The city is building on this momentum. It is well placed to develop an aeronautics cluster, strengthen its 
role as a hub for social impact and further expand its distinctive creative industries , with industry  
remaining at the heart of its economy. To support this ambition, the municipality is developing a  
professional system for attracting and facilitating investment.
OUR CHALLENGE
To attract outstanding companies and talent, positioning the municipality as a driving force for national 
and international development.
WHY THIS IS YOUR OPPORTUNITY
As an investor, you need a location where setting up and growing a business is straightforward, efficient 
and transparent. The municipality is committed to providing exactly that environment.
- Direct access to decision-makers;
- Established business and industrial areas, with significantly more land becoming available;
- A distinctive pool of skilled talent;
- Proximity to Lisbon, Portugal’s economic centre and an international technology hub;
- An excellent quality of life, with access to housing, education and healthcare;
- Access to EU investment incentives that can be more attractive than those available in the capital.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 4
ALIGNED WITH THE EUROPEAN UNION’S REINDUSTRIALISATION 
STRATEGY
Competitiveness Compass;
Clean Industrial Act;
Industrial Accelerator Act;
SAFE — Security Action for Europe.
A MUNICIPAL LEADERSHIP TEAM WITH BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
Attracting investment is central to our vision for the municipality. The Mayor and Deputy Mayor are both 
entrepreneurs who entered public service to help transform Caldas da Rainha. They understand the  
challenges of running a business and the importance of private initiative. After years of improving  
municipal procedures, the city is ready to take a more prominent place on the investment map. Our  
executive  team  combines  practical  business  experience  with  a  clear  understanding  of  what  the  
municipality needs to succeed.
PARTNERS YOU CAN TRUST
Foreign direct investment in Portugal remains encouraging, and there is broad national agreement on  
its importance. However, investors still face challenges, including complex administrative procedures  
and regulations that are not always business-friendly. We understand how important it is for businesses 
to have reliable partners at both technical and political levels . Partners who act transparently, meet  
deadlines and are accountable for results.
A HISTORY OF INNOVATION
Caldas da Rainha was founded on innovation. In the late 15th century, Queen Leonor established a  
thermal hospital that combined the distinctive qualities of the local waters with a commitment to care for 
all. Its mission was laid out in a written charter, the Compromisso, with clear rules and objectives. This  
pioneering initiative helped define the city’s character: bold ideas supported by lasting commitments.
In the late 19th century, innovation took a new form. Under the influence of Rafael Bordallo Pinheiro,  
ceramics challenged conventions and reached new markets. Creativity, humour and social satire were  
combined with industrial production, establishing Caldas da Rainha as an international reference and  
creating a network of talent that endures today. Throughout the 20th century, the city developed a  
diversified economy, with resilient traditional retail in its centre, industries ranging from cutlery to  
machinery and equipment, and services including logistics and distribution.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 5
KEY SECTORS — Industry
WE ARE INDUSTRY
Design, creativity and a distinctive product identity help businesses stand out in global markets. In  
Caldas da Rainha, this is more than a theory. The Strategic Economic Development Plan (PEDE 2035) 
brings  together  industry,  the  creative  sector  and  innovation  in  a  single  cluster.  It  is  one  of  the  
municipality’s most significant economic clusters, comprising 911 establishments, approximately 3,800  
jobs (17.9% of local employment) and €354 million in turnover. Between 2017 and 2022, it outperformed 
the Oeste regional average in business activity, employment and company growth [1].
Talent  underpins  this  cluster.  The  municipality  has  eight  higher-education  graduates  per  1,000  
inhabitants, above the national average [2]. ESAD.CR, a school of art and design established in 1990,  
plays a central role in developing that talent. Within a compact urban area, graduates and entrepreneurs 
can find spaces to create and work: SILOS – Contentor Criativo, located in a former flour mill since 2010; 
Prontos. and its Impact Village, offering coworking and incubation; the Centro de Artes; and Teatro da  
Rainha [3]. Caldas da Rainha has been a UNESCO Creative City of Crafts and Folk Art since 2019.
An industry driven by creativity
Caldas da Rainha has developed an industrial model built on originality. It combines a strong identity,  
design, technology and manufacturing expertise. Ceramics is a prime example. Bordallo Pinheiro  
demonstrates how industrial heritage and contemporary design can reinforce each other, while Molde,  
Braz Gil Studio and a new generation of studios are following a similar path. The cutlery industry, where 
family businesses have grown into global brands, shows that this model extends well beyond ceramics. 
The municipality’s skilled workforce has also attracted international engineering, tooling and equipment 
companies. Supporting this ecosystem is an unusually strong technical training network for a city of this 
size. CENCAL trains ceramics technicians, while CENFIM specialises in metalworking and automation. 
Secondary  schools  also  offer  vocational  courses  in  IT,  robotics,  electronics,  automation  and  
mechatronics.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 6
Ready for Industry 5.0
The European Commission has outlined a new vision for manufacturing: Industry 5.0. Automation and  
digitalisation, central to Industry 4.0, are no longer sufficient on their own. The industry of the future must 
put people first, operate within environmental limits and be resilient to disruption. Caldas da Rainha has 
a distinctive set of skills and capabilities to contribute to this model.
The three pillars of Industry 5.0
Human-centricity: putting people at the heart of production, with technology supporting workers and 
freeing them from repetitive tasks.
Sustainability: using resources more efficiently, reducing environmental impacts and embracing the 
circular economy.
Resilience: preparing companies and organisations to withstand supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical 
instability and extreme weather.
A people-centred industry depends on professionals who combine practical skills with creative thinking, 
talent Caldas da Rainha has cultivated for generations.  But resilient businesses also need resilient  
infrastructure. In the first half of 2026, for example, the municipality managed a sharp increase in urban 
waste without disruption to services. This capacity to respond effectively to pressure is an important  
advantage for investors. The municipality also plans to invest more than  €8 million in upgrading  
wastewater  treatment  facilities  for  the  next  decade.  Urban  regeneration  projects  are  moving  
infrastructure networks underground to improve their resilience. New business areas are being designed 
to balance everyday mobility with freight transport and to benefit from highly connected fibre-optic  
networks.
For  investors,  the  result  is  a  location  combining  skilled  talent,  a  strong  industrial  base,  resilient 
infrastructure and openness to new opportunities.
Sources: [1] PEDE Caldas da Rainha 2035 – Diagnostic Report (EY-Parthenon, 2025), section 4.3, 
pp. 47–50. [2] Ibid., section 2.2, pp. 20–21. [3] silos.com.pt; prontos.pt; rpac.pt. Industry 5.0: European 
Commission, "Industry 5.0 – Towards a sustainable, human-centric and resilient European industry" 
(2021).

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 7
KEY SECTORS — Aeronautics
A unicorn has landed. More are welcome!
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 1.
Caldas da Rainha was chosen by a leading developer of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as the  
location  for  its  development  and  production  centre.  Its  strategic  Euro-Atlantic  position,  suitable  
infrastructure and ability to attract and retain talent make it an ideal setting for growth. The municipality  
is  an  active  partner  in  the  company’s  expansion.  Current  planning  and  investment  are  creating 
opportunities for a wider aeronautics cluster with international reach.
The company is already a major anchor for the region, with a drone pilot training school and facilities  
dedicated to aircraft engine development. A runway and additional facilities are planned in Caldas da  
Rainha over the coming years, expanding its capacity for local operations and growth. The municipality 
is working with the relevant national authorities to identify effective solutions for the area, the company  
and prospective investors.
The municipality considers aeronautics a strategic priority and aims to contribute to the national strategy 
for the sector, strengthening its role in an increasingly important international industry.
IN FOCUS
Caldas da Rainha is home to the engineering centre of TEKEVER, the Portuguese drone manufacturer 
that became the country’s first defence-tech unicorn in 2025. Its unmanned aircraft are designed here  
before undertaking missions across Europe and beyond.
TEKEVER chose Caldas da Rainha for its skilled workforce, quality of life and location approximately  
one hour north of Lisbon. Its success demonstrates that a mid-sized Portuguese city can support world-
class deep-tech businesses.
The growing network of engineers, suppliers and specialist expertise surrounding TEKEVER creates  
opportunities for other technology companies seeking to scale from this region.
KEY FIGURES
2025 — Portugal's first defence-tech unicorn
≈400 — people at TEKEVER's engineering centre
≈1 hour — from Lisbon

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 8
KEY SECTORS — Ceramics Industry
Innovation Powered by Heritage.
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 3.
THE CLUSTER THAT MOULDS THE CITY
Ceramics has shaped Caldas da Rainha for centuries. Today, it forms a complete ecosystem rather  
than a single industry. Alongside Bordallo Pinheiro, the city’s industrial base includes Molde, founded in 
1988, which launched its own brand of tableware, decorative pieces and tiles made from locally sourced 
fine stoneware in 2018 [1]. Braz Gil Studio, a family-owned porcelain manufacturer founded in 1996,  
produces luxury pieces and reproductions for palaces and museums [2]. Design-led producers such as 
Duro Ceramics combine handcrafted techniques with contemporary collections for international buyers  
[4]. They build on the legacy of SECLA, whose studio brought together prominent Portuguese artists  
during the second half of the 20th century [3].
CENCAL, the ceramics industry’s vocational training centre since 1981, trains technicians and operates 
an accredited ceramics laboratory. ESAD.CR teaches product design specialising in ceramics and glass. 
A new generation of ceramic artists, including young people and international newcomers, is opening  
studios, galleries and independent shops [5]. MESTRA, the city ’s ceramics market, brought together  
more than 110 ceramicists in 2026 [6]. The Museu de Cer âmica, the Rota Bordaliana and the city ’s 
UNESCO Creative City designation, held since 2019, complete this ecosystem. For investors, the city  
offers suppliers, skilled labour, research and development capabilities, and an active creative market, an 
ideal environment for new brands, design-led manufacturing and materials innovation.
Sources: [1] Molde, supplier profile at Formland. [2] Braz Gil Studio, "Our History", brazgil.pt. [3] 
Associação Portuguesa de Cidades e Vilas de Cerâmica, "Caldas da Rainha". [4] Duro Ceramics, 
Maison&Objet brand page. [5] CNN Portugal, 15 Jun. 2025. [6] Tinta Fresca, 1 Jun. 2026.
IN FOCUS
Since 1884, Bordallo Pinheiro has helped reinvent ceramics in Caldas da Rainha. Rafael Bordallo  
Pinheiro challenged the conventions of his time through satire, nature-inspired forms and colour.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 9
Today, the company bearing his name, part of the Vista Alegre Group, continues to transform that  
heritage  into new  creations. By reissuing historic moulds, working with contemporary artists and  
designers, and reaching markets across Europe, the United States and Japan, Bordallo Pinheiro  
connects tradition with innovation.
It remains a living platform for innovation, supported by skilled craftspeople, the CENCAL ceramics  
training centre and the nearby design school.
KEY FIGURES
1884 — Bordallo Pinheiro
Europe · US · Japan — international markets
CENCAL + ESAD.CR — training + design ecosystem

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 10
KEY SECTORS — Cutlery Industry
Sharp skills. Global reach.
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 5.
Cutlery is one of Caldas da Rainha’s lesser-known export success stories. IVO Cutelarias began in the 
1940s, when a craftsman sold razors from his bicycle.
Today, the family-owned company, based in Santa Catarina, produces around five million knives a year 
and exports almost all of them to more than 90 countries.
Its success reflects one of the region ’s strengths: precision metalworking expertise developed over  
generations and supported by training at CENFIM.
Here, family businesses have transformed traditional craftsmanship into globally recognised industrial  
brands. Suppliers, toolmakers and new entrants can benefit from an established supply chain and an  
experienced workforce.
KEY FIGURES
≈5 million — knives produced per year
90+ countries — export markets
1940s — origins of IVO Cutelarias
IN FOCUS
CALDAS CUT https://www.caldascut.com/about-event.html
CALDAS CUT marks an important opportunity to strengthen international partnerships and encourage  
the exchange of technical and artistic expertise. It also promotes the Made in Portugal label as a symbol 
of precision, durability and design in global markets.
Cutlery is a strategic sector for the Portuguese economy. With annual exports of around €48.6 million, 
Portugal is a major European supplier to demanding markets including Germany, France and Canada.  
The Oeste region, particularly Caldas da Rainha and Alcobaça, is at the heart of the industry, accounting 
for more than 40% of national production.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 11
KEY SECTORS — Retail
Where the street is the marketplace.
In Portugal, a city whose streets are full of people is a city full of life. In Caldas da Rainha, streets connect 
communities and public squares serve as shared gathering places , a natural home for independent  
shops. Retail and services are major drivers of the local economy, accounting for 4,498 establishments 
(55.9% of the total), approximately €1.25 billion in turnover (63.9%) and 54.9% of local employment [1]. 
In recognition of this vibrant commercial environment, the European Commission named Caldas da  
Rainha the 2026 European Capital of Small Retail in the Vibrant City category, selecting it from 28 cities 
across 13 countries. This distinction complements the city ’s UNESCO Creative City status, held since  
2019.
RETAIL 5.0 · A Caldas da Rainha model
High-street retail does not compete with online shopping by copying it. It succeeds by offering what  
digital channels cannot provide on their own, while using technology to improve efficiency. Retail 5.0  
puts technology at the service of people: digital tools enhance personal relationships rather than replace 
them. Caldas da Rainha is developing a new generation of hybrid retail built on three pillars.
People. Personal relationships are the greatest strength of local retail. Caldas da Rainha is investing in 
welcoming, personalised and increasingly professional service that understands customers, offers  
expert advice and creates experiences no online platform can replicate.
Digital. Behind the counter, operations are evolving through digital processes, pedestrian footfall data to 
inform opening hours and campaigns, and a multilingual online marketplace connecting local shops with 
customers worldwide.
Logistics.  Customers can shop in person and receive their purchases at home, or order online and  
collect them in the city centre. Smart lockers and delivery services connect physical shops with digital  
customers while encouraging visits to the high street.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 12
From "Retail 4.0" to Retail 5.0
In Retail 4.0 (2018), Philip Kotler and Giuseppe Stigliano describe how digital technology moves beyond 
a separate sales channel to become part of the entire shopping experience. They identify ten principles 
for retail in this new era:
Be invisible: technology simplifies shopping without being noticed.
Be uniform: the same experience across all channels, physical and digital.
Be a destination: the shop has to give people reasons to go there.
Be loyal: build lasting relationships of trust.
Be close: know the customer and personalise.
Be a curator: select and advise, don't just sell.
Be human: the personal relationship remains decisive.
Be inexhaustible: surprise and renew the offer.
Be exponential: use data and platforms to grow.
Be brave: take risks and innovate.
Caldas da Rainha is taking this concept further. Retail 5.0 combines the digital integration of Retail 4.0  
with an additional dimension: the city itself. Participatory governance, urban regeneration and retail-
focused public policy can make the entire commercial centre a destination, rather than relying on  
individual shops alone [2].

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 13
Bairro Comercial Caldas da Rainh@
The Bairro Comercial is a key driver of this model. It brings together a digital marketplace, smart lockers, 
pedestrian footfall sensors and training programmes. Its governance is participatory: the municipality,  
AIRO, ACCCRO and local retailers work together through the Living Council of Retail & Services and  
initiatives such as Caldas com Alma and Loja Verde. The neighbourhood is increasingly becoming a  
testing  ground  for  urban  retail  policies,  where  new  solutions  can  be  evaluated  before  wider  
implementation. Local identity further strengthens the ecosystem, with seven shops recognised by the  
Comércio com História network, the Rota Bordaliana and major events including MESTRA, Feira dos  
Frutos, Caldas Nice Jazz, Caldas Late Night and Bazar à Noite.
Praça da Fruta
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 7.
Praça da Fruta is the “operating system” of retail in Caldas da Rainha: an open-air market in the central 
square, brought to life every day by local producers and traders. It is a place where commerce and  
history come together.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 14
IN FOCUS
LET US HELP YOU FIND YOUR "SECRET INGREDIENT"
Every successful business has a secret ingredient, and so does every city. In Caldas da Rainha, ours is 
there for those who know where to look: distinctive buildings ready for new uses, welcoming streets on  
a human scale and a community that grows with newcomers. The city increasingly welcomes local  
initiative and participation. This summer, Bazar  à  Noite, an independent market organised by an  
association, brought together 56 creators and encouraged nearby shops to stay open later. Projects  
attract people, people form communities and communities create opportunities for new businesses. Now 
we are looking for your ingredient: the idea, concept or brand that makes your business unique. Our  
team can help you find the right space, street and partners to bring it to life. Shall we explore the right  
formula for your business in Caldas da Rainha?
CALDAS DE AUTOR - Concepts for Investors
A regional retail hub: Help position Caldas da Rainha as the leading retail destination between Lisbon 
and Leiria.
Distinctive brands: Build the next brand with national reach, following examples such as Sportino in 
retail or Fitness Factory in services.
Food and dining: Combine international cuisines with local flavours, beginning at Praça da Fruta.
Independent design: Open galleries and independent shops showcasing work by emerging ESAD.CR  
designers, following examples such as Laboratório d’estórias.
Urban regeneration: Introduce new retail concepts in distinctive buildings, a future Creative District or  
neighbourhoods beyond the established commercial centre.
SOURCES
[1] Municipality of Caldas da Rainha, European Capital of Small Retail application (INE data, 2022).
[2] P. Kotler and G. Stigliano, Retail 4.0. 10 regole per l'era digitale (2018); Spanish edition: Retail 4.0. 
10 reglas para la era digital (LID Editorial, 2020); English edition: Redefining Retail.
[3] CNN Portugal, 15 Jun. 2025, "Há uma tribo de artistas que está a usar a cerâmica para transformar as Caldas da Rainha".
[4] Gazeta das Caldas, 17 Sep. 2026, "Bazar deu destaque à cerâmica local".

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 15
KEY SECTORS — Tourism
AN AUTHENTIC AND GROWING DESTINATION
Caldas  da  Rainha  lies  at  the  heart  of  one  of  Portugal ’s  strongest  tourism  regions.  Peniche  is  
internationally renowned for surfing, Nazar é  for its giant waves,  Óbidos for cultural tourism and the  
Monastery of Alcobaça for its UNESCO World Heritage status. Caldas da Rainha offers attractions of  
its own: a historic thermal spa tradition, the Óbidos Lagoon, popular with kitesurfers, and Foz do Arelho, 
where an Atlantic beach meets a sheltered lagoon. The city also offers a year-round cultural programme 
through venues including the Centro Cultural e de Congressos, Centro de Artes, Museu de Cer âmica 
and Museu Jos é  Malhoa, alongside contemporary creative activity at ESAD.CR and SILOS. The  
emphasis is on sustainable, distinctive tourism rather than mass tourism.
The figures show the opportunity:
Growing demand: the city recorded 207,225 overnight stays in 2023, up 12.0% from 2017, nearly twice 
the national growth rate of 6.6% [1].
Demand outpacing supply: accommodation supply increased by 50%, reaching 30 establishments and 
1,670 beds, but demand is growing faster. The PEDE recommends expanding accommodation capacity 
[1].
Potential for higher-value tourism: revenue per available room (RevPAR) stands at €27.6, compared 
with €40.4 in the Oeste region and €64.8 nationally. With an average stay of 2.0 nights, there is scope  
for more high-quality, higher-value accommodation [1].
Established specialisation: tourism and the local economy form the municipality ’s only cluster with a  
higher concentration of activity than both the Oeste region and Portugal as a whole [1].
Image: municipal postcard collection (14 October), p. 13.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 16
Where to invest: the PEDE identifies four areas [1]:
thermal spa and wellness;
creative tourism linked to ceramics and art;
business and events tourism (MICE);
integrated offers with Óbidos, Nazaré and Peniche.
Strategic alignment: these investment areas reflect the priorities of Turismo Centro de Portugal for 2020–
2030, including wellbeing, business tourism and lifestyle [2]. The Centro 2030 framework recognises  
Caldas da Rainha as a UNESCO Creative City and includes plans to strengthen thermal and slow  
tourism, as well as establish a Convention Bureau for the Centro region [3].
Investor support: the Escola de Hotelaria e Turismo do Oeste develops skills for the regional tourism  
sector [2]. Turismo de Portugal offers support programmes, financing options and the potential tax  
benefits associated with Tourist Utility status [4].
Sources: [1] PEDE Caldas da Rainha 2035 – Diagnostic Report (EY-Parthenon, 2025), pp. 43–46 and 
71–73. [2] Turismo Centro de Portugal, Regional Tourism Development Plan 2020-2030. [3] Turismo 
Centro de Portugal, Turismo Sustentável Centro 2030 – Strategic Framework (2023). [4] 
business.turismodeportugal.pt.
Foz do Arelho · Alexey Komarov · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 17
KEY SECTORS — Health and Wellbeing
A city founded on care.
Caldas da Rainha was founded on a tradition of care. In the late 15th century, Queen Leonor established 
a thermal hospital here, one of the oldest institutions of its kind in the world. Today, this heritage is  
helping shape a new economic sector. In October 2026, the University of Leiria and Oeste opened a  
health  sciences  campus  in  the  city,  initially  offering  courses  in  thermal  spa  services,  wellbeing,  
cosmetics,  healthy  nutrition  and  laboratory  sciences.  Degree  programmes  in  digital  health  and  
biomedical laboratory sciences are awaiting accreditation. Major private healthcare providers and an  
active social-impact community further strengthen the local ecosystem. Caldas da Rainha welcomes  
investment in wellbeing, health technology and social innovation.
Image: municipal postcard collection (14 October), p. 11.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 18
KEY SECTORS — Design
Design that changes the game.
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 9.
In Caldas da Rainha, design does more than shape appearances: it changes how businesses operate. 
Since 1990, ESAD.CR, the School of Art and Design, has trained designers, artists and makers in the  
city. Its research laboratory, LiDA, worked with a leading glass manufacturer to develop one of the  
lightest wine bottles on the market. The project received a Red Dot Design: Best of the Best award in  
2026. This is an example of design reshaping a product, its supply chain and an industry. Caldas da  
Rainha has been a UNESCO Creative City of Crafts and Folk Art since 2019. Creative hubs such as  
SILOS and Prontos. help retain local talent. For investors, the city offers access to designers, prototyping 
facilities and research partners capable of transforming both products and business processes.
KEY FIGURES
- 1,600 — art and design students (ESAD.CR)
- up to 80% recycled glass
- more than 30% less glass
- 40% lower carbon emissions
2026 — Red Dot Design – Best of the Best
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
LIDA - Laboratório de Investigação em Artes e Design | Laboratory in Design and Arts
LiDA, based at the School of Art and Design, received an Excellent rating in an evaluation by the  
Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT). It conducts research in design, art and culture.
Its mission is to advance applied research, experimental development and knowledge transfer in support 
of a more sustainable future. To achieve this, LiDA works with businesses, museums, non-governmental 
organisations and national and international research institutions that share its objectives.
Sources: LiDA, lida.pt; Universidade de Leiria e Oeste, FCT evaluation results published on 15 April 2025: https://www.ipleiria.pt/fct-atesta-
elevada-qualidade-das-unidades-de-investigacao-do-ipleiria/

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 19
TALENT — The City and the University
Minds in Action.
Image: municipal postcard collection (VF), p. 13.
In Caldas da Rainha, ideas do not stay on paper. Prototyping, making and practical problem-solving are 
embedded in education, from secondary school to university. The city has eight higher-education  
graduates per 1,000 inhabitants, compared with a national average of seven. ESAD.CR trains designers, 
artists and makers in well-equipped studios and laboratories, turning creative thinking into practical  
expertise. In October 2026, a new health sciences campus expanded the city ’s educational offer.  
Specialist training centres provide industry with a steady flow of skilled workers: CENCAL for ceramics, 
CENFIM for metalworking and automation, and the Oeste Tourism School for hospitality. Vocational  
schools further strengthen the talent pool through courses in software, networks, renewable energy and 
mechatronics. For investors, this means access to creative, technically skilled professionals who are  
prepared to solve real-world challenges.
The recently established University of Leiria and Oeste, successor to the Polytechnic Institute of Leiria, 
has reinforced Caldas da Rainha’s position as a university city. Alongside its internationally recognised  
School of Art and Design, the city now hosts a campus of the university’s School of Health.

CALDAS DA RAINHA   /   INVESTOR GUIDE
Next Opinion · Município de Caldas da Rainha 20
SCHOOL OF HEALTH CAMPUS of the University of Leiria and Oeste
In October 2026, the university opened a School of Health campus in Caldas da Rainha, initially  
welcoming  approximately  80  students  across  four  higher  professional  technical  programmes:  
Aesthetics, Cosmetics and Wellbeing; Thermal Spa and Wellbeing; Forensic and Criminal Laboratory;  
and Healthy Eating. Two degree programmes — Digital Health and Biomedical Laboratory Sciences — 
are under review by A3ES and could expand the offer in the coming years. The focus is on wellbeing,  
care and disease prevention, complementing nursing and health technology programmes in Leiria. For  
investors, this creates access to technicians trained in thermal spa services, cosmetics, nutrition,  
laboratory analysis and digital health.
ESAD CR | School of Art and Design of the University of Leiria and Oeste
ESAD.CR is a teaching and research institution located at Campus 3 in Caldas da Rainha. It has around 
1,600 students and more than 130 lecturers. Its four-building campus was designed around studios and 
workshops. Facilities cover ceramics and glass, wood, metalworking, printmaking and screen printing,  
photography, audiovisual production, theatre, digital fabrication and 3D prototyping. The school offers  
eight bachelor’s degrees: Fine Arts; Spatial Design; Product Design – Ceramics and Glass; Graphic and 
Multimedia Design; Industrial Design; Cultural Programming and Production; Sound and Image; and  
Theatre. It also offers master’s degrees in Sound and Image Arts, Fine Arts, Product Design, Graphic  
Design and Cultural Management, along with higher professional technical programmes in digital  
prototyping, graphic production, digital media and audiovisual production. ESAD.CR also provides a  
public cultural programme of exhibitions, talks, artistic residencies and performances.

PELICAN VALLEY
The pelican is one of the city’s symbols. It appeared in the coat of arms of King João II (1481–1495) and 
was  associated  with  the  charitable  values  that  shaped  the  foundation  of  the  Thermal  Hospital.  
Traditionally, the pelican is depicted nourishing its young by sacrificing part of itself — a symbol of care 
and dedication.
Pelican Valley is a bold vision inspired by the city ’s growing private investment in healthcare, its  
established social-impact community and new investment in technology. Together, these strengths offer 
the foundations for a distinctive cluster of innovation and impact.

shared entrepreneurship ecosystem. The programme offers free acceleration initiatives, consultancy,  
mentoring and a network of service providers offering preferential terms. It also includes physical  
incubation and coworking facilities, along with a digital platform designed to attract digital nomads to the 
region.
UpCaldas
UpCaldas is an incubation, acceleration and coworking hub developed by AIRO and the Municipality of 
Caldas da Rainha. Based at Expoeste, it forms part of the Startup Oeste ecosystem. Its first phase  
opened in November 2025 with 12 coworking places. Officially inaugurated on 12 June 2026, the  
expanded hub includes an auditorium, 14 private offices, 20 flexible coworking places, training rooms  
and leisure areas, with round-the-clock access. It serves local entrepreneurs, growing SMEs and remote 
workers, while also aiming to attract digital nomads to the region.

SOFTLANDING — Infrastructure and 
Networks
Energy — a strength of the municipality
Transmission grid (REN). The 400 kV Ferreira do Alentejo–Pegões–Rio Maior line terminates at REN’s 
Rio Maior substation and crosses the municipality of Caldas da Rainha through the parish of Vidais.  
According to REN, construction is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2025, with completion  
expected in October 2027. The project is primarily intended to transmit renewable electricity generated  
in southern Portugal [1]. For energy-intensive businesses, proximity to an extra-high-voltage network is 
an advantage, although it does not guarantee available connection capacity.
Distribution grid (E-REDES). E-REDES operates the medium- and low-voltage electricity distribution  
network. Its Caldas da Rainha facilities opened in 2019 and comprise a building of approximately 6,500 
m² employing 77 people [2].
Grid access for major consumers. Decree-Law No. 120/2025 amended the exceptional procedure for  
allocating  electricity  connection  capacity  in  designated  high-demand  areas,  including  a  financial  
guarantee [3]. Applicable procedures and available capacity must be confirmed with the relevant network 
operator. The municipality cannot guarantee connection capacity.
Fibre-optic network — national backbone and local access
National backbone (IP Telecom, part of the Infraestruturas de Portugal group). IP Telecom operates  
more than 6,780 km of fibre-optic cable nationwide and offers redundant network infrastructure [4]. The 
modernisation  of  the  Oeste  railway  includes  signalling  and  telecommunications  works  [5].  The  
availability of commercial fibre services for a specific property must be confirmed with operators.
Local access (FTTH). In 2024, Vodafone extended its fibre network to three parishes in the municipality: 
Carvalhal Benfeito, Salir de Matos and Santa Catarina. The latter includes an industrial area [6].  
Coverage and connection terms must be confirmed with the network operators for each site.
Regional context. ANACOM reported that FTTH adoption in Oeste e Vale do Tejo was above the national 
average in the second quarter of 2025 [7]. Regional adoption figures do not establish coverage at an  
individual business site.
What this means for companies with large data volumes or data centres
Strength: proximity to major electricity and railway infrastructure, together with telecommunications  
networks,  can  support  data-intensive  operations.  Each  project  requires  confirmation  of  electricity  
connection capacity, commercial fibre availability and redundancy at the proposed site.
Opportunity: small and medium-sized regional or edge data centres, disaster-recovery facilities serving 
businesses in Lisbon, and industries requiring data-intensive processing.

who speak French, Spanish and other languages. Although a medium-sized European country, Portugal 
shares a language spoken by around 300 million people worldwide.
